semantics.note: The normalization correctly resolves last year to 2024 and preserves the strict threshold.

contract.note: The passage expressly includes noncash expenses. Net loss is a fair ordinary measure of the inclusive economic loss asserted here, although the speaker supplies no formal accounting definition.

evidence.note: Reports full-year 2024 net loss above $5 billion on the relevant inclusive basis, before the evaluation cutoff.
Provides independent corroboration of the financial documents. Its rounded 2024 figure neither establishes nor contradicts the strict greater-than threshold.

attribution.note: Both financial-effect assertions are Zitron's own.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the categorical no-benefit assertion and the qualified stronger assertion of harm.

contract.note: Incremental revenue and costs fairly operationalize the asserted financial effect. The launch-period reading fits the surrounding discussion; the evidence gap persists under broader readings.

evidence.note: OpenAI discloses compute intensity, not product profitability. This company disclosure supplies neither attributable revenue nor a comparison without Deep Research.

reviews.rationale: The categorical assertion that Deep Research contributes nothing toward profitability is assessable. Compute intensity alone cannot establish its incremental financial effect. The packet lacks attributable revenue, retention, costs and a defensible counterfactual, so neither the no-benefit assertion nor the stronger negative effect is established.

contract.note: Testing whether exaggerated representations principally drove investor decisions fairly captures the causal assertion without inventing a numerical threshold.

evidence.note: Confirms reporting of the proposed transaction but supplies no investor explanation establishing its principal valuation drivers.
A later investor disclosure describes its broad thesis. It neither establishes the February proposal's principal cause nor demonstrates that relevant representations were exaggerated.

reviews.rationale: The packet establishes the reported fundraising proposal and provides a later investor thesis. It does not establish which representations were materially exaggerated or their importance relative to other investment considerations. Neither support nor contradiction of the principal-cause allegation follows.

attribution.note: The annual-increase assertion is Zitron's own, distinct from the management forecasts he quotes.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves both companies and the every-year quantifier without adding a cash-only restriction.

contract.note: The contract restricts burn to cash consumption, although this case's revision explicitly identifies a broader usage including noncash costs. The surrounding cash discussion makes that reading plausible but does not justify imposing it exclusively.

evidence.note: The timely company filing documents increased Anthropic operating cash use from 2023 to 2024. Its accounting basis and limited coverage cannot establish the broader claim. The 2025 decrease falls outside the claimed period.

reviews.rationale: The frozen cash-only contract does not fairly preserve the broader burn scope identified in this case. A consistent measure is needed before grading. Even under the contract's reading, the packet supplies only one relevant annual comparison for Anthropic and no comparable OpenAI series; later declines cannot contradict a claim ending in 2024.
